title: Stop FirestoreGatewayImpl.pushGoal from using non-idempotent add() for id-less goals

evidence.quote:
final id = goal['id']?.toString() ?? goal['goal_id']?.toString();
    if (id != null) return id;

why: Every other push* method here (pushCompletion, pushStreak, pushTrack, pushLedgerEntry...) derives a deterministic Firestore doc id so an outbox retry after a lost ack is a safe overwrite via set(merge:true). pushGoal is the one method that falls back to collection.add() -- a fresh random doc id -- whenever the payload carries no id/goal_id. outbox_sync_write_facade.dart's own _goalKey fallback (a composite curriculum_pct_timestamp key) proves this null case is real, not theoretical: it exists specifically to dedupe local enqueues of such goals. If the server commits the add() but the client never sees the ack (timeout, dropped connection -- exactly what the outbox's at-least-once retry exists to survive), the retry calls add() again and creates a second, permanent duplicate goal document in Firestore, which the pull path then merges back down as a duplicate goal locally.
recommendation: Assign every goal a stable id before it is ever enqueued (mirror the ULID pattern already used for streak/ledger/points-ledger entries) and have pushGoal always do doc(id).set(merge:true); delete the add() branch.
acceptance_criteria: Regression test: call pushGoal twice with an id-less payload against a fake/emulator Firestore; assert exactly one document exists afterward.
pushGoal's add() branch is removed or provably unreachable.

refutations: Traced every real producer of pushGoal payloads: GoalRepositoryImpl._syncGoal (data['id']=entity.firestoreId), LocalDataUploadService's goal-upload loop (payload['id']=firestoreId), and TutoredWriteRouter (pass-through of the same payloads) — all three ALWAYS inject the deterministic firestoreId get
corrections: Downgrade to P2/SUSPECTED design-debt, not a live P1 defect: the add() branch and the docId-null path are dead code under every existing caller (goal_repository_impl.dart, local_data_upload_service.dart both always set a deterministic id first). The finding's "_goalKey fallback proves this is real" claim is incorrect — that fallback is itself unreachable. The residual risk is real but latent: nothing type-enforces that a future goal-creation path must set id, so the add() fallback remains a landmine, and it literally violates FB-4's "never add()" text. Recommendation (delete the add() branch, assign ids unconditionally) is still sound as defensive hardening, just not as an active data-integrity bug happening today.

Both current call sites (goal_repository_impl.dart:242 via _syncGoal, local_data_upload_service.dart:185) always set data['id'] to a deterministic, non-null firestoreId before calling pushGoal, so the add() branch and the outbox_sync_write_facade.dart _goalKey null-id fallback are both currently unreachable dead code, not live retry-triggered duplication risk as the "why" claims.

Evidence quotes are accurate verbatim, but the reachability claim is wrong: _goalKey's fallback in outbox_sync_write_facade.dart is generic defensive coding (mirrors the pattern in _key for other entities), not proof the null-id branch fires in practice — every actual call site sets data['id'] before pushGoal is invoked.
